description: Pre-registered labels and protocol for the Elastic Security Labs real-report attribution benchmark (docs 21.3.4c). Only slugs, ATT&CK ids and our own paraphrases are stored here; the post text is downloaded by scripts/prepare_elastic_reports.py into data/benchmarks/elastic/ (gitignored, local evaluation only, (c) Elastic).

protocol.headline: reports below, strict anonymization, local pipeline, every kept sentence read as the product's no-LLM mode reads a pasted report
headline_metrics: top1 as k/n with a Wilson 95% interval
arms: strict with 30 seeded-random sentences, seeds 1-5 (volume diagnostic)
protocol.open_set: stage distribution, names given and which groups, apt_like vs commodity, combined named risk with the labelled reports, how often each group leads open-set rankings
protocol.rules: scripts/report_anonymizer.py and scripts/prepare_elastic_reports.py as committed with this file; labels and rules are not changed after results are seen without a logged reason; nothing is tuned on this set
protocol.not_claimed: no significance test against CTI-HAL (disjoint groups, different reading regime); strict removes victim geography too

selection: Screened all 302 feed posts (May 2022 - Sep 2026) for attribution to a group in ATT&CK 19.2, then adversarially verified each candidate; kept only Elastic's own attribution of real observed activity with enough behaviour prose. Umbrella/sub-group ambiguity is recorded in accept, fixed before any run.

reports.basis: Elastic's own attribution from code and string overlap with public reporting on the group's malware and shared C2 paths; Lazarus Group is not accepted because ATT&CK 19.2 keeps the two apart and links them nowhere
attribution_sections: DPRK attribution: why this links to Contagious Interview
